description: The PL-270 settlement corpus: one Work's three Measurement Books, the three IWRCMS railway bills raised from them, and the three tax invoices raised against those bills. Recorded so the MB -> bill -> invoice closure chain has a regression bar drawn from real documents rather than from assumptions.

provenance.work: PL-270, Central Railway Mumbai Division (S&T), supply and installation of train information display boards

chain_head.note: The Letter of Acceptance that starts this Work is ALREADY in the repository as an LOA parser fixture. It is not duplicated here; the settlement corpus continues the same document's life. The owner's copy of the LOA was checked against it and is byte-identical once CRLF is normalised.
chain_head.signature_note: The LOA carries no digital signature at all. It is a browser print of the IREPS page -- the extracted text still holds the print header 'ireps.gov.in/epsn/works/tds/publishLOAWorksLetter.do' and a timestamp. LOAs are deliberately NOT in the gated set, which is consistent with this: the document operators actually hold is a print, not a signed original.

redaction_note: The three human signatories are third parties (two Central Railway officers and one contractor signatory). Their names are replaced in the extracted text with role pseudonyms -- CONTRACTOR SIGNATORY, RAILWAY ENGINEER REP, RAILWAY SR DSTE -- because nothing under test depends on them. This is stricter than the LOA corpus, which records 'verbatim-names-retained'. Everything structural is verbatim: identifiers, dates, quantities, amounts, GSTINs, IRNs and the signature reason strings. The source PDFs are NOT in this repository and must not be; certificate material stays out of git entirely.
trap_notes: The measurement number links MB to bill by SEQUENCE, not by string equality: an MB carries its own 'On Account Measurement No. .../OAM/L2/NN' while the bill that consumes it references '.../OAM/FL2/NN'. The L2 -> FL2 prefix change is not an error. Matching these documents on the raw measurement string will silently fail to link every pair.
An MB also back-references the PREVIOUS bill's FL2 number (MB-2 carries FL2/01, MB-3 carries FL2/02). Do not assume the only FL2 token in an MB is its own bill.

The measurement number WRAPS across lines in -layout output of the bills ('.../CSTM/11393' then '16/OAM/FL2/01' on the next line). Any extractor must rejoin it before matching, the same hazard the LOA parser contract records for wrapped units.
Bill amounts are GST-INCLUSIVE ('Rate is inclusive of GST: Yes'). The invoice taxable value is the bill total divided by 1.18; the bill total equals the invoice GRAND total, never its taxable value.

The bill total is whole rupees while the invoice carries paise, and they do not always agree exactly: BILL-3 states 17327888 against an invoice total of 17327888.01. A closure check that requires exact equality will refuse a legitimate settlement. Compare at rupee granularity, or allow at least one paisa.
The invoice may be dated BEFORE its bill (INV-1 is 09/05/2026 against a bill dated 11/05/2026) and its IRN may be registered before the bill is fully signed. Do not enforce invoice_date >= bill_date.

executed_value_rule.ruling: Owner ruling, 2026-08-13: LOA rates are USUALLY GST-inclusive at 18% total, works contracts in India falling in the 18% slab -- but SOME LOAs quote GST-exclusive rates. It is rare, and it does happen.
executed_value_rule.therefore: The GST basis is a PER-WORK ATTRIBUTE captured from its LOA, never a constant in code. Default to inclusive, record what the LOA actually says, and compute executed value on the recorded basis. A hardcoded 1.18 is a latent defect that stays invisible on every ordinary work and then misreports the rare one.
executed_value_rule.why_it_matters: Executed value drives work completion, and a work may be marked completed only at 100% executed value.
executed_value_rule.the_dangerous_direction: Assuming inclusive when an LOA is actually exclusive compares GST-inclusive bill totals against a GST-exclusive contract value and OVERSTATES execution by 18%. Such a work reads 100% executed at about 85% of its real value, so it can be marked completed while roughly a sixth of the contract is still unbilled. The opposite mistake merely holds a finished work open, which is visible and annoying rather than silent and wrong.
executed_value_rule.the_arithmetic: Compare like with like. Once the basis is known, executed value is the same percentage whether computed GST-inclusive (bill totals against Net Bid Value) or GST-exclusive (invoice taxable values against Net Bid Value / 1.18), because both sides scale by the same factor. What must never happen is MIXING the two bases -- which is the natural mistake, since bills state a GST-inclusive figure while invoices state a taxable one.
executed_value_rule.evidence_for_this_work: PL-270 is an inclusive LOA. The bill states 'Rate is inclusive of GST: Yes' and its Agreement Rate column derives from the LOA schedule, so the LOA schedule carries the same basis. The LOA letter itself is silent on GST -- searching PL270-CRB.txt for 'inclusive of GST', 'GST extra' and similar returns nothing -- which is exactly why this cannot be read off the letter and must be captured as an attribute.

worked_example_pl270.note: The two consistent bases agree to four decimal places. The mixed figure is out by exactly the GST wedge -- 29.4874 / 24.9893 = 1.18 -- which is what makes it recognisable when it happens.
